page: Microsoft Azure B8s_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine instance within the Bsv2 family, engineered for workloads requiring variable CPU performance. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance operates on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading, coupled with 32 GB of system memory to maintain a balanced 4 GB per vCPU distribution. The CPU features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The B8s_v2 instance is Premium Storage capable but does not package bundled local storage, requiring attached external storage for persistent volumes. It also contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs. In synthetic benchmarking, the server demonstrates baseline performance across typical computational tasks, achieving 1,642 in Geekbench single-core and 6,114 in multi-core testing. Memory throughput registers at 55.96 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 38.86 GB/sec for writes. While single-threaded compression and general integer execution remain competitive within the median tier of cloud servers, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yields lower relative performance compared to non-burstable alternatives.

Operating under a burstable allocation framework, the B8s_v2 offers strong qualitative cost efficiency by trading continuous maximum CPU utilization for the ability to absorb periodic computational surges. Sustained heavy compute can exhaust burst capacity, making non-burst architectures preferable for flat, continuous batch processing. Consequently, the instance is structurally suited for environments with fluctuating demand, such as software compilation pipelines, code repositories, intermediate testing clusters, lightly loaded databases, and web application backends.
description: Microsoft Azure B8s_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine designed for workloads that experience intermittent spikes in resource utilization. Powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor, the instance provisions 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores alongside 32 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Architectural capabilities include AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. The instance does not include local disk storage, relying on attached remote block volumes for persistence. Benchmark evaluation shows performance centered in the average tier across single-core and multi-core CPU metrics, memory bandwidth, and static web serving, with lower throughput observed in parallel decompression tests. Due to its burstable allocation model, the instance delivers a cost-efficient deployment profile for non-sustained CPU workloads. It is appropriately configured for build and compilation servers, staging environments, intermediate databases, and web applications with variable traffic patterns.
